text: 🍿 Netflix just handed Sheridan's most underrated show a second life All four seasons of Mayor of Kingstown hit Netflix on October 5, right before the final season. Taylor Sheridan co-created it, and it's the one nobody talks about next to 'Yellowstone' . 🎬 Honestly, that's a shame. Jeremy Renner as a fixer holding a prison town together is bleak, pulpy and a little overcooked, and I mean that as a compliment. It won't win awards, but 40 episodes of grim, well-oiled pulp is a very good fall binge. 🔥 ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Endgame takes the crown back, by a hair 'Avengers: Endgame' is the highest-grossing movie ever again, edging out 'Avatar' by roughly $2 million (about $2.9255B to $2.9237B, per Deadline). A re-release pulled it off, and the timing is no accident. I like the cheek of it. The Anthony and Joe Russo movie gets a victory lap right before 'Avengers: Doomsday' lands in December, which is smart marketing. It also feels a bit like a stat built for a headline. 🤔 James Cameron won't sit still, and his sequels and re-releases make this a seesaw. Enjoy the throne while it lasts. ✈️ Add to watchlist

🎬 Spider-Noir dies after one season, and it makes no sense Prime Video pulled the plug on 'Spider-Noir' with 92% on Rotten Tomatoes and 11 Emmy nominations, the most of any of its shows this year. Nicolas Cage finally got his first regular TV role, and it shows he can carry a series. My read is that it launched big but dropped out of the top 10 fast, and the price tag didn't help. Black-and-white and color versions of every episode is a gorgeous flex, just not a cheap one. That's the lesson from the 'Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse' era that streamers keep ignoring. Weird Spider-Man works. Weird Spider-Man at prestige-drama cost apparently doesn't. 🕷️

🍿 The Social Reckoning has a legs problem, and I'm not sure Sorkin cares 📆 Release: October 9, 2026 🎭 Genre: #Drama · #Biopic ✈️ Add to watchlist Tracking points to an $8 to $13 million opening, against the $22.4 million that 'The Social Network' pulled in back in 2010. Soft for something this splashy, and it means the film lives or dies on word of mouth. 📉 Me compra que Aaron Sorkin directs it himself, and Jeremy Strong and Mikey Madison are a serious pair. Me chirría the October slot for an adult drama with no Fincher. Ojo, this one needs critics to carry it. 🎬
